notes: The gotchas pack does what its README says. Its single pass reads sessions, the matched note and the transcript turns that mention it. It runs once per note, only on notes matching **/Gotchas*.md and **/Pitfalls*.md, and gets work when a session names or links such a note, as the README describes. It proposes only appends under a final `## Logged gotchas` section. The prompt treats all inputs as untrusted data and forbids quoting commands, instructions or links that only tool output shows. It keeps entries to what the cited turns establish and caps the size of each proposal. The 'how to avoid the trap' part of an entry is part of the stated purpose and must come from the cited turns. The reviewer persona rejects by default, checks every entry against the evidence, rejects agent instructions, commands or links that the turns do not show or that come only from tool output, and keeps a strict JSON reply format. The template holds only a short description and an empty section heading, with no instructions, commands, links or credential handling. The fixtures are clearly synthetic: they are marked synthetic and use a sample CLI and a neutral allotment note that checks the path filter. No hidden, encoded or misnamed content and no injected instructions were found.
